title: Reduce config churn by normalizing profile defaults
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Runtime now normalizes effective config defaults to the profile-pack canonical defaults (when a hardware tuning profile is selected). This reduces repeated diffs/churn in logs and makes rollbacks more predictable. No API changes.
description:
Context: As part of the hardware tuning profiles pack, we currently have two sources of “defaults”: (1) the profile pack JSON (intended to be the canonical recommended settings per SKU/mode) and (2) runtime hard-coded defaults (historical behavior, plus some safety values for missing keys). In practice this causes drift and churn: a profile may omit a key assuming the runtime default, or the runtime default changes for unrelated reasons, and the *effective config* changes even though the profile version did not. This shows up as noisy config dumps, confusing perf regressions, and painful rollbacks.

This PR refactors default handling so that when a profile is selected, the runtime produces a normalized effective config where unspecified keys are filled from the profile pack’s declared defaults (not from runtime hard-coded defaults), and the runtime hard-coded defaults are used only as a last-resort safety net for truly unknown keys / older packs.

What this changes: The effective config becomes stable across runtime releases as long as the profile pack version is pinned, and it becomes stable across profile updates because normalization makes “absence vs explicit default” consistent. This should materially reduce config churn in startup logs and make canary comparisons cleaner.

Scope: No behavioral changes when no profile is selected (runtime defaults remain the source of truth). No new knobs introduced. This is primarily a normalization/precedence refactor and migration support.

Related: ENG-4822 (schema/validation), ENG-4823 (loader/override order), pr-21984 (schema + validation), pr-21991 (profile selection).
commits: 1) runtime/config: introduce canonical default map sourced from profile pack metadata 2) runtime/config: add normalizeEffectiveConfig() to fill unset keys + canonicalize booleans/ints 3) runtime/config: preserve override precedence while normalizing post-merge 4) runtime/logging: reduce noisy diff output; log normalized effective config hash 5) tests: add golden tests for normalized output across H100/L40S example profiles 6) docs: add migration notes + troubleshooting section for config churn
changed_files: runtime/config/profile_pack_loader.cc (applyDefaults + normalization path); runtime/config/effective_config.cc (new normalization function); runtime/config/schema/profile.schema.json (adds optional defaults block + clarifies semantics); runtime/config/validation/profile_validation.cc (ensures defaults are type-correct + within guardrails); runtime/logging/startup_config_log.cc (logs normalized config + hash); runtime/tests/config/test_effective_config_normalization.cc (golden tests); docs/internal/runtime/hardware_profiles/migration_notes.md (new); tools/config_dump/README.md (updates expected output semantics)
testing: Unit: runtime-config-tests (added normalization golden tests). Integration: profile-loader-integration-tests (override precedence unchanged). Manual: ran runtime with H100 balanced profile on perf-canary dev pool; verified startup logs show stable normalized config (hash identical across restarts).
rollout_plan: 1) Land behind internal flag RUNTIME_NORMALIZE_PROFILE_DEFAULTS=1 for one release train cycle. 2) Enable in canary pools (H100 us-east, L40S us-west) and verify config-hash stability + no perf regression. 3) Remove flag after 1 week of green canary; keep safety net for older profile packs for at least 2 minor runtime versions.
migration_notes:
Operationally visible changes:
- When a profile is selected, `effective_config` output will now include keys that were previously omitted (because they were implicitly runtime defaults). These keys will be set to the profile pack’s canonical defaults.
- Startup logs now include `runtime.effective_config.hash` computed after normalization. Use this for comparing deployments rather than raw JSON diff.
- If a customer has out-of-band overrides that relied on “missing key implies runtime default”, behavior should remain consistent because overrides still apply, but the printed config will be more explicit.

Compatibility:
- Older profile packs that lack a `defaults` block: runtime falls back to existing runtime defaults (no change from current behavior). A warning is logged once per boot: `profile_defaults_missing=true`.
- Newer profile packs: `defaults` is validated and used for normalization.

Rollback:
- Set RUNTIME_NORMALIZE_PROFILE_DEFAULTS=0 to revert to previous behavior (prints less explicit config; may reintroduce churn). No data migrations required.
discussion:
Benji Okafor: “Can you clarify where normalization occurs relative to override order? We can’t accidentally ‘default-fill’ and then have later override logic treat those values as user-provided.”
Ethan Park (author): “Normalization is applied after we compute the merged config (runtime baseline + profile + overrides), but it only fills keys that are unset/absent in the merged config. Overrides remain authoritative; normalization does not mark values as overridden.”

Quentin Harris: “We should avoid breaking older profile packs. How do we detect pack version capabilities?”
Ethan Park: “We added a capability bit from the parsed pack metadata (`supports_defaults_block`). If absent, we skip profile-default normalization and log a one-time warning so operators know they’re not getting the churn reduction yet.”

Paula Mendes (SRE): “Please add a crisp way to compare ‘did the config change’ between canary/control without doing JSON diffs.”
Ethan Park: “Added `runtime.effective_config.hash` and included it in the startup compatibility log line. Also updated runbook snippet in the internal docs.”

Diego Santos: “Private deployments dump config via Helm hooks; ensure this doesn’t explode diffs on upgrade.”
Ethan Park: “It will become more explicit, so diffs may show more keys once. After that, it should stabilize. Added migration notes + recommended comparison using the hash.”

Follow-ups agreed in thread:
- Add a small helper in the CLI dump tool to print only non-default overrides (tracked separately).
- Consider promoting config-hash panel to the rollout dashboard (Observability pack PR forthcoming).
